items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Count Basie had been through here and had given us several beautiful scores by Hugo Winterhalter, Buster Harding, and several other arrangers.

ctx.x: And then we opened up the last part of the season of '41 at the Club Plantation. The same band. In

1942, -- anyway, 1942 was a good year for the band, personnel-wise. And it was good from the music standpoint because Count Basie had been through here and had given us several beautiful scores by Hugo Winterhalter, Buster Harding, and several other arrangers. And this helped our repertoire. We kept rehearsing the band, and we tried to inject some original ideas into these various arrangements that we had.

In the meantime, there was a program on every Sunday afternoon called the Fitz Bandwagon program. And they would advertise from various cities throughout America, the most popular band in that territory. So we decided to get in the contest. There was a drug company in St. Louis called Meyers Drug Company. They were the key people in the city of St. Louis representing NBC and the agency -- advertising agency who had the account for the Fitz Bandwagon people.
